nt.trang.he: According to the Yellow Emperor's Inner Classic (Ling Shu, chapter on the Five Colours), {ten} corresponds to {he}. Changes in skin colour here usually mean changes in daily rhythm (sleep, food, stress) — face reading only reminds you to take care and have regular check-ups; it does not diagnose illness and is not medical advice.
nt.trang.tuoi_td: Which ages the yearly-position book reads in this area
nt.trang.tuoi: The yearly positions of fortune divide the face into 100 positions by traditional age; {ten} corresponds to ages {ds}. Men look at the left side first, women at the right side first. Where the area is full and bright, that age goes easier; where it has lines or is dark, that age calls for more initiative — it is the books' way of looking, not a forecast.

nt.trang.chinh_xac_hoi: Is reading your own face accurate?
nt.trang.chinh_xac_dap: A face you observe yourself is always truer than one someone else reads; this page only speaks about tendencies and habits, not about what will happen.
